newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica shares end quiet day weak ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica shares end quiet day weak ahead of holiday.

text.p: South African shares ended weak in listless trade on Monday, with industrials easing amid a lack of interest and golds depressed by a softer bullion price.
Dealers said the market had almost ground to a standstill in the afternoon ahead of the Heritage Day public holiday on Tuesday and on the Jewish Yom Kippur holiday on Monday.
"Trade is non-existent. We have done about a quarter to a third of normal turnover today. It is absolutely static...We had a bit of trade up to lunch, but after lunch it was dead," a dealer said.
Overall index shed 17.4 points to 6,917.9 points, industrial index was down 19.9 points to 8,170.9 points and gold index fell 16.5 points to 1,721.4 points.
